name: Volumetric Scattering Model
definition: Volumetric scattering refers to light scattering in volumetric phenomena like clouds, smoke, fire, and translucent materials like wax and human skin. The medium responsible for the scattering is called a participating medium. Without volumetric scattering, the radiance along a straight ray between two surfaces is constant; with participating media, the media affect the radiance along the ray.
